answer: An honest AI agent must invest 1 unit of verified labor to complete a task, while 1,000 fakes must incur 1,000 units to achieve parity, ensuring operational costs remain non-amortizable. The system emits a ripple of task-specific input challenges, requiring each agent to return a crystal-clear output derived from the unique pre-state. The verifier caches these proofs within a yarrow-indexed database to discard any duplicate submission. If an audit detects a fraudulent mismatch between state transitions, it triggers an immediate identity revocation. This assumes tasks are non-shareable.
